title: Duration of Sessions
summary:
The chapter says each session should last long enough to give benefits without causing excessive fatigue. Appropriate duration supports cardiovascular capacity, helps control pregnancy weight, eases lower back pain, sciatica and muscle tension, and improves mood, energy and stress.

Aerobic sessions of 20-30 min add up to at least 150 min of moderate activity per week, while strength and flexibility work can be done in 15-20-min sessions two to three times per week. Duration should be adjusted by trimester and by the woman's profile (sedentary, active, athlete), staying flexible according to tolerance and symptoms. Excessive fatigue is a sign to reduce duration or intensity.
points: Aerobic sessions are suggested at 20-30 min, accumulating at least 150 min of moderate activity per week.
Strength and flexibility exercises can be done in 15-20-min sessions, two to three times per week.
In the first trimester, women could start with shorter sessions and gradually lengthen them according to tolerance.
In the second and third trimesters, avoid prolonged sessions without rest, especially long periods of standing.
Sedentary women should start with 15-20-min sessions and build to 30 min, adding 5 min each week up to 30 or 40 min.
Sedentary sessions can be split into 10-15-min blocks if needed to support adherence.
Active women can maintain 30-45-min sessions and should alternate strength and aerobic days if not doing multi-component sessions.
Pregnant athletes can maintain 45-60-min sessions, divided into aerobic and strength blocks with adequate rest and active recovery.
Duration should be flexible, depending on tolerance, symptoms and trimester.
takeaways: Aim for 20-30-min aerobic sessions toward the 150 min weekly total.
If you are new to exercise, start at 15-20 min and add 5 min per week.
Split sessions into 10-15-min blocks when that helps you keep going.
Alternate strength and aerobic days to avoid fatigue when not combining them.
Take rests and avoid long periods on your feet in later trimesters.
Treat heavy fatigue as a cue to shorten or ease sessions.
cautions: Excessive fatigue indicates duration or intensity should be reduced; consult a healthcare professional if necessary.
Avoid prolonged sessions without rest in the second and third trimesters.
